content:
As I see it, we're only using it to keep track of goals generated by the proof mode, in ProofModeM.State.goals, instead of having them in TacticM.State.goals. What's the purpose of keeping them appart though?

cc @Michael Sammler
I guess a more broad question is: how does ProofModeM differ fromTacticM?
Hmm, ok, I'm reading parseIrisGoal? and I tink I get it a bit
These mvars represent holes to the right of some Entails'. And this separation is useful because otherwise one doesn't have access the the extra Hyps hypothesis in their context

One of the main functionality that ProofModeM provides is the special tracking of goals. In particular, the addBIGoal function and friends. This means internal functions of tactics can just call this function to add a goal. Internal functions cannot just directly manipulate TacticM.State.goals since this would be very hard to keep track of which function manipulates the goals in which ways. Instead, ProofModeM collects all new goals and adds them all (in a specifically sorted way) at the end of the tactic. See the end of ProofModeM.runTactic for this. Before ProofModeM, each tactic hand rolled its own version of this collection of new goals.

The other main functionality is the parsing of the Iris Goal. In general, ProofModeM collects all the boilerplate necessary for writing an IPM tactic.

But in the end, ProofMode.runTactic only does some postprocessing on them later and then dumps them in the same list of all other goals in TacticM.State, right? Isn't this equivalent to just having something like 

let oldGoals ← get
setGoals []
-- Execute tactic here
let goals ← getGoals

The main reason I started looking into it is because I had assumed that ProofModeM overloaded TacticM with some extra tracking of contexts of goals which live in some PROP with a BI PROP, since this information cannot be found directly in the mvars context. However, it seems like this information is only provided to the ProofModeM.runTactic closure and must be transported from one function to another.

Would it be possible to add some kind of mapping to ProofModeM.State between MVarIds and Hyp instances? That way we can access the mvarid given to ProofModeM.runTactic's instance by doing some variant of getGoal, and maybe add some getSpatialHypothesis or getIntuitionisticHypothesis that operate on MVarIds, and get access to the fields in IrisGoal.

In principle, one can always simulate a lot of this with getGoals / setGoals / replaceMainGoal. But as a maintainer, I think the important point is the abstraction boundary. If every proof-mode helper directly manipulates the raw TacticM goals, then every helper has to correctly implement the same discipline: save the old goals, clear or replace the current goals, collect the newly generated BI goals, restore the old goals, and apply whatever postprocessing/sorting/invariants we want. If one helper forgets to use the right replacement operation, or leaves goals in the wrong place, the resulting behavior becomes very hard to reason about.

About the map, I think that it is much more delicate than it sounds. The parsed IrisGoal/Hyp data is a view of the current target at a particular moment. It is not intrinsic data stored in the metavariable context. Tactics can transform goals, assign metavariables, close goals, create new goals, or identify/merge metavariables through unification. Then the map can easily become stale.

Fernando LEAL said:

Would it be possible to add some kind of mapping to ProofModeM.State between MVarIds and Hyp instances? That way we can access the mvarid given to ProofModeM.runTactic's instance by doing some variant of getGoal, and maybe add some getSpatialHypothesis or getIntuitionisticHypothesis that operate on MVarIds, and get access to the fields in IrisGoal.

I am sorry, but I don't understand what you mean here. There is no correspondence between hypothesis in the proof mode context and mvars, so I am not sure what mapping you are referring to. The hypothesis are available via the Hyps data structure that is provided by ProofModeM.runTactic. Not sure what the purpose of the getSpatialHypothesis or getIntuitionisticHypothesis functions would be.

Yunsong Yang said:

But as a maintainer, I think the important point is the abstraction boundary.

I agree about this usecase. Actually, I believe that it makes sense to have a ProofModeM which is distinct from a TacticM because they are inherently different concepts, even if currently the implementation of one is done in terms of the other. I just expected its actual behaviour to differ from TacticM since it was implemented explicitly as a separate datatype, but as it stands I don't see the current definition being any different from having

def ProofModeM := TacticM

Michael Sammler said:

Not sure what the purpose of the getSpatialHypothesis or getIntuitionisticHypothesis functions would be.

In Lean we have that each MVarId is assigned some metadata in the MetavarContext over at MetaM.mctx through a series of persistent maps, in particular MetavarContext.decls mvid |>.lctx has the local definitions which are available to build mvid under, right? I was just thinking whether we could have a similar version to this, where ProofStateM.State has a persistent map from mid : MVarId to the hyps : Hyp bi e for which we have hyps.tm |- mid as a goal.
And then, functions such as getSpatialHypothesis could be built so they get the associated Hyps bi e of some metavariable mid through the monad, instead of needing to pass them explicitly

Yunsong Yang said:

Then the map can easily become stale.

I don't understand what you mean by "the map becoming stale". Isn't the only mutation done to a metavariable done when a metavariable is assigned to an expression? I don't think this would make entries in the mapping stale. Could you give an example?

Fernando LEAL said:

where ProofStateM.State has a persistent map from mid : MVarId to the hyps : Hyp bi e for which we have hyps.tm |- mid as a goal

I guess this wouldn't really be a ProofStateM.State anymore, but more a ProofTermM.State, which is more analogous to an extended MetaM than an extended TacticM.
(deleted)

Sorry, I am not understanding what you are proposing at a very basic level. You refer to Hyp but there is no type of this name. Do you mean Hyps? But then you refer to something called getSpatialHypothesis, which sounds like it would return a single hypothesis, but then you say it returns a Hyps so multiple hypotheses?

You also talk about a correspondence between mvar and Hyps, but there is no such correspondence between them as far as I see. E.g. Hyps.split turns one Hyps into two Hyps, but there are no changes to mvars involved.

Maybe you want to add more indirection through some state? But what would be the point of this? (Adding more indirection usually makes things more complex, so I think it is better to avoid.)
How would you rewrite for example the isplitl tactic under your proposal?
Hmm
I mean Hyps when I said Hyp, sorry. As you can probaby tell, the time between thinking and writing has not been much in these past few messages :P

I think it is good to have discussions like this to understand the code and the design space better. I am happy to discuss alternate designs. If you have some insights / explanations that help you understand the current code better, feel free to also create PRs that add these as documentation somewhere in the code such that people in the future will have an easier time understanding what is going on.

Fernando LEAL said:

Yunsong Yang said:

Then the map can easily become stale.

I don't understand what you mean by "the map becoming stale". Isn't the only mutation done to a metavariable done when a metavariable is assigned to an expression? I don't think this would make entries in the mapping stale. Could you give an example?

I think the issue is that the Iris hypotheses are not independent objects attached to the metavariable. They are already encoded in the target of that metavariable.

So if I understand your proposal correctly, you want something like a map from an MVarId to the corresponding Iris hypotheses, whether spatial or intuitionistic. But those hypotheses are obtained by parsing the current target. They are not separate stable variables that can be split off from the goal and tracked independently.

This is why I said the map can become stale. It is not necessarily because the MVarId itself is mutated in some complicated way. Rather, after applying a tactic, the entire target of the metavariable may change. The Iris context you previously parsed was a view of the old target, so even if that view was correct before, it may no longer describe the current goal.
By target you mean the type of the metavariable, or the expression assigned to it?

Also, it is true that I was thinking we could assign to an Iris goal a metavariable, when this is in fact not true, since goals in Iris are not types, but instances of some PROP type, and a metavariable stands for a typed expression. But I'm less interested about the implementation of this interface, and more about the interface. And, in short, I would like to be able to work with Iris terms as I would work with Lean terms.

Maybe an illustrating example may help to communicate what I mean. While implementing iLöb I wanted to implement an equivalent to _iRevertIntrosCore which would deal with the forall argument. And I would like the API of this method to be something like revertingTelescope (hs : List SelTarget) (k : ProofModeM a) : ProoModeM a. As it stands, however, there is no way to access the hypothesis of the current goal from whithin the ProofModeM monad (other than parsing the main goal's types again). This is the sort of usecase I would like to support with my original proposal of adding persistent maps to ProofModeM.State.
So maybe it's enough to have ProofModeM := ReaderT IrisGoal $ StateRefT State TacticM? Having all of IrisGoal as the context seems wrong to me, maybe just hyps is enough
But then, I would also argue for ProofModeM := ReaderT IrisGoal TacticM, since ProofModeM.State and TacticM.State serve the same purpose

Yunsong Yang said:

In principle, one can always simulate a lot of this with getGoals / setGoals / replaceMainGoal.

About this, I couldn't remember the idiomatic way of doing this, but I believe I have found it, it's focus

Fernando LEAL said:

So maybe it's enough to have ProofModeM := ReaderT IrisGoal $ StateRefT State TacticM? Having all of IrisGoal as the context seems wrong to me, maybe just hyps is enough

So your proposal is to make the current IrisGoal implicit instead of explicitly passed? I have thought about this when designing ProofModeM, but decided against this design since the tactic implementations make a lot of use of the fact that the proof mode is explicit instead of implicit. In particular the parameter e of the Hyps often appears in the signature of functions. This means that the construction of proof objects in Lean is actually checked statically using Qq, preventing one common source of problems which can happen in the implicit version / Rocq version. (I.e. in Lean we get a lightweight version of something like MTac for free)

Also many tactics do not manipulate an IrisGoal, but Hyps and goal separately. This works well with the explicit version, but would become a lot harder with the implicit version. This gives a lot more flexibility to the tactic implementation. See for example the implementation of iframe. In general, the Iris Lean tactics work quite differently from the Rocq tactics: The Rocq tactics always have this implicit state of the IrisGoal, while in Lean the tactics have the hyps and the goal explicit and can manipulate them more freely and explicitly.

You can write your revertingTelescope function, you just have to explicitly talk about Hyps and the goal. See the other tactics for how to do this.

Fernando LEAL said:

since ProofModeM.State and TacticM.State serve the same purpose

No, the two states do not serve the same purpose. TacticM.State is manipulated by all tactics and linked to the info view and so on. ProofModeM.State collects the goals generated by an IPM tactic before they are added to TacticM.State at the end of an IPM tactic such that the goals can sorted into dependent and non-dependent goals.

I mean, the purpose of both states are still to keep a list of goals. That ProofModeM gives it additional semantics through ProofModeM.runTactic in that it reorders goals around doesn't change that. I also don't see the benefit of keeping these separate from Tactic.State.goals, this kind of separation is already supported by the existing TacticM API

Michael Sammler said:

This means that the construction of proof objects in Lean is actually checked statically using Qq, preventing one common source of problems which can happen in the implicit version / Rocq version.

It is true that Iris Lean makes heavy use of Qq, which might explain all of these discrepancies. But then we differ from Lean's tactic APIs, which are much more stateful generally. I was expecting ProofModeM to provide a similar interface, which is what got me surprised at first.

I'm not sure yet whether both features are incompatible, however. One could build an API closer to Lean that still leverages Qq
If you have a concrete proposal for how to redesign the API of ProofModeM and some examples of how the existing tactics would look like with the redesigned API, I would be happy to discuss it.
Yes, I agree that discussing this without nothing implemented is just wasting time
Let's see what I come up with

I ended up finishing the iloeb PR using the current ProofModeM API. I'm not super happy with the way in which I compose tactics, but I don't know how I could have done it better (other than maybe returning more information from the other tactic's functions).

This ended up taking much more time than I originally wished, so I have decided to postpone my proposal for an alternate ProofModeM API until after I have finished with weakestpre.v.
